**Type:** DOCUMENT

**Source:** work-006-design-phase-skills -> delivery-003

**Depends on:** task-070

**Scope:**
- Source: `features/feature-006-integration-and-close-out/SPEC.md` §7's `kb.html` sub-section and its
  §10 rows *`kb.html` regenerated, not patched* (four conjuncts) and *Not asserted here: an automated
  visual gate*; PLAN.md cross-cutting risk 5; and the owner decision recorded in REQUIREMENTS §4. It
  closes BLUEPRINT criterion **10**.
- **It is its own task and it is last, and both are decisions rather than conveniences.** The run reads
  `.aid/knowledge/{doc}.md` for every resolved document
  (`canonical/skills/aid-summarize/references/state-generate.md` §2), so a run started before the
  Knowledge Base refresh is final bakes in the pre-refresh figures. And it is a long authored run, not a
  command: the last recorded full GENERATE took **24m20s** and produced a 178 KB / 20-section file
  (`.aid/knowledge/STATE.md` § Calibration Log, the 2026-06-25 `aid-tech-writer (summarize GENERATE)`
  row), corroborated by the § Summarization History row for the same date. Size it accordingly.
- **The premise that this file could not be regenerated is false and was corrected.** `tech-debt.md`
  `W1-11` claimed the assembler's `.aid/.temp/summarize/` input tree no longer exists; in fact GENERATE
  reads the Knowledge Base directly and **writes** that tree itself during the run -- skeleton, per-doc
  section files and `section-manifest.txt` (§5) -- which
  `canonical/aid/scripts/summarize/assemble.sh` then concatenates into `.aid/knowledge/kb.html` (§8).
  `.aid/.temp/` is gitignored scratch (`.gitignore:69`), so its absence between runs is the expected
  end-state of the previous run, not a missing input.
- **`kb.html` is not hand-patched.** Hand-editing an assembled artifact makes it neither current nor
  reproducible, and the next assembler run silently overwrites the edit. That is also why it is the
  only route that closes mode **M6**: the count guard's `EXT` filter admits no `.html`
  (`check-skill-counts.mjs:170`), so no `CLAIMS` entry can ever reach this file and task-069 correctly
  did not try.
- **What is stale, measured rather than recalled.** `grep -c '75 skills' .aid/knowledge/kb.html` is
  **3** today and `grep -c '58-row'` is **2**; `grep -c '34 verb-first'` is **2** and that figure is
  **correct today and stays correct** -- the regeneration must reproduce 34, not move it. The file was
  already two roster generations stale before this work began.
- **The visual gate is an orchestrator step, and this task does not promise otherwise.**
  `canonical/aid/scripts/summarize/validate-visuals.mjs` exists but is SKIPPED, because Playwright is
  not installed in the summarize package -- `.aid/knowledge/STATE.md` § Knowledge Summary Status,
  **Visual-Gate Note**: *"V1 visual gate must be run by the orchestrator"*. What this task asserts is
  the **machine half** plus an explicitly **orchestrator-run** V1 verdict recorded in
  § Summarization History like every prior run. A criterion claiming a passing automated visual gate
  would be a criterion that cannot run.
- **`W1-11`'s `kb.html` half closes here**, in the same pass, because it closes exactly when the
  regeneration lands. The entry stays **open** on its other survivor, `W1-2`'s hand-measured per-shape
  populations, which are still prose. task-067 moved `W1-11`'s two live figures and deliberately left
  this half open.
- **One self-reference this task states rather than resolves.** The `W1-11` closure and the
  § Summarization History row both *describe the run that just produced `kb.html`*, so neither is
  reflected in `kb.html` itself, and the `tech-debt.md` edit lands after `INDEX.md` was regenerated. No
  ordering resolves that; what the task does instead is check whether `INDEX.md`'s summary of
  `tech-debt.md` actually changed, and re-run `build-kb-index.sh` if it did. `INDEX.md` is therefore
  declared as a write of this task, conditionally exercised.
- Out of scope: an automated visual gate; hand-patching `kb.html`; adding `.html` to the guard's `EXT`;
  any Knowledge Base document's content beyond `tech-debt.md`'s `W1-11` closure and `STATE.md`'s new
  history row; and `relationships.md` / `graph.html`.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] **BLUEPRINT criterion 10, conjunct (a) -- M6 is cleared.**
      `grep -c '75 skills' .aid/knowledge/kb.html` captured to a variable -> `0` (it is `3` today) and
      `grep -c '58-row' .aid/knowledge/kb.html` -> `0` (it is `2` today), with the new figures present
      instead: the corpus total reads **112** and the catalog reads **94** rows
- [ ] **Conjunct (b) -- the negative half, in the same file.**
      `grep -c '34 verb-first' .aid/knowledge/kb.html` captured to a variable is still **>= 1**. This is
      the **third independent witness** that the `shortcuts` (emitting) quantity did not move -- a
      generated file, so it cannot be talked into agreement -- and a regeneration that swept it off 34
      fails here
- [ ] **Conjunct (c) -- produced by the assembler, not edited.**
      `.aid/.temp/summarize/summary-src/section-manifest.txt` exists from **this** run; its non-blank,
      non-`#` line count equals the resolved doc-set count taken from `.aid/settings.yml` **+ 2** (the
      `00-at-a-glance` opener and the trailing KB index, neither a document section --
      `state-generate.md` §5's ordering rule); and `kb.html`'s section anchors appear in that manifest's
      order. The `+ 2` is not assumed: § Summarization History records 18 docs -> 20 sections and 19 docs
      -> 21 sections
- [ ] **Conjunct (d) -- the run is recorded.** A new `## Summarization History` row in
      `.aid/knowledge/STATE.md` carries the output size, the section count and the **orchestrator-run**
      V1 verdict, in the existing seven-column shape
      (`| # | Date | Grade | Profile | Mermaid | Output | Notes |`). § Knowledge Summary Status is
      updated in the same pass -- Last Run, Output, Doc-Set Count and Human Grade
- [ ] **Conjunct (a) alone is not accepted as evidence, and the record says why**: (a) passes on a
      hand-patch and (c) passes on a run started before the Knowledge Base refresh, which is why all
      four conjuncts are required and why this task is ordered last
- [ ] **The automated visual gate is NOT claimed.** The record states that `validate-visuals.mjs` was
      SKIPPED, names Playwright's absence from the summarize package as the reason, and reports V1 as an
      **orchestrator** verdict with who ran it and what they checked. A record that reports a passing
      automated visual gate fails this criterion even if the page renders correctly
- [ ] **`W1-11`'s `kb.html` half is closed and its other survivor is still open.** The `W1-11` entry no
      longer names `kb.html` as a survivor, still names `W1-2`'s prose populations, and `W1-2` itself is
      untouched: `git diff HEAD -- .aid/knowledge/tech-debt.md` shows no change to the `W1-2` row
- [ ] **The `INDEX.md` self-reference is resolved by checking, not by assuming.** After the
      `tech-debt.md` edit, `bash canonical/aid/scripts/kb/build-kb-index.sh` is re-run and
      `git diff --exit-code -- .aid/knowledge/INDEX.md` is checked; if the index changed, the
      regenerated file is committed and the change is recorded. Either outcome is acceptable; not
      checking is not
- [ ] **The run's cost is recorded against its band.** A new `## Calibration Log` row in
      `.aid/knowledge/STATE.md` carries the agent, the cycle, the ETA band and the actual elapsed time,
      so the ~24-minute figure this task was sized against is either confirmed or corrected for the next
      run
- [ ] **Only the declared paths moved.** `git diff --name-only HEAD` lists `.aid/knowledge/kb.html`,
      `.aid/knowledge/tech-debt.md`, `.aid/knowledge/STATE.md` and -- conditionally --
      `.aid/knowledge/INDEX.md`, and nothing else. `.aid/.temp/` is gitignored and is not committed
- [ ] Accuracy verified against the current codebase: the three `grep -c` baselines are re-measured
      before the run so the after-values are compared against a live before-value, and every path and
      section name cited is re-resolved against the tree as it stands
- [ ] Nothing outside the declared writes moves:
      `git diff --exit-code -- canonical/ tests/ site/ docs/ profiles/ .claude/ .cursor/
      .aid/settings.yml` is clean
- [ ] All section-6 quality gates pass
